newsitem.title: POLAND: INTERVIEW - Agros issue to up production.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Agros issue to up production.

text.p: The forthcoming issue of 2.425 million shares at 70 zlotys each by Polish food trader and producer Agros SA should help the company add production firms to its holding, Agros' president said on Tuesday.

Zofia Gaber told Reuters that about half the funds from the offering, which starts on Thursday and lasts to March 26, would go toward buying firms in the meat, sugar, grain or fats industries and to lift stakes in current subsidiaries.
Gaber said one of the purchases could be edible fats maker Kruszwica SA, as Agros had made the treasury ministry's short list for up to a 46-percent stake.
"We're on the shortlist for Kruszwica and currently in the final stage of negotiations...which could last several more weeks," Gaber said in an interview.
Kruszwica's president has said the ministry would likely pick an investor by the end of the first quarter.
Gaber said the 70-zloty price announced on Monday, which came from a book-building range between 65 and 80 zlotys, took into consideration recent falls on the Polish and other European bourses.
The Warsaw bourse fell 6.6 percent from Thursday to Monday before rebounding on Tuesday.

Gaber said the high interest in the firm's shares during the recent Western European road show suggested the role of the underwriting consortium led by Austria's Creditanstalt Investment Bank AG could prove limited.
She reiterated that large Western institutional investors could become passive investors in the 1.24-million-share institutional tranche on March 20 and 21.

"The book-building interest suggests the role of underwriters won't be significant," she said, adding she was cheered by the firm's Tuesday bourse performance, when Agros fell 1.4 percent to 73 zlotys with strong post-fixing buying.

"If people today are buying at 73 (zlotys) even though they know the (new-issue) price of 70, that means the price 70 is (seen as) a special price for a limited number of shares and that the (bourse) price will quickly go up," she said.
Gaber said the firm should lift its 27-percent fruit-juice market share over the next few years faster than that market's expected annual growth of 20-25 percent.
The firm plans for production to grow to about two thirds of its sales by the year 1999 from about 50 percent currently.

Gaber also said that though Poland's state-owned Polmos distillery firms could fall within the natural orbit of Agros' activities, it was too early to discuss buying one as the treasury ministry had yet to announce a privatisation plan.
